note: The recovery record. Append-only: every attempt to find the authoritative wording of a rule, with what was searched, how, and what came back. It exists so that SOURCE_MISSING is an auditable conclusion rather than an assumption, and so that nobody has to run the same search twice.

searches.method: grep of every tracked file for rule numbering and rule phrases
searches.result: No rule wording found. The repository contains only the tracker's own code and data.
Only the tracker's own commits exist; no imported rule material.

searches.method: git grep for "rule", rule numbering, "project rules", "development rules"
searches.result: No rules document exists anywhere in the EJE checkout.

searches.method: git cat-file over all 1544 blobs under 400KB across all 91 commits, searched for rule phrases and for numbered rule-like lists reaching 11+
searches.result: Zero matches. No rules register has ever existed in the EJE repository.

searches.source: docs/SCOPE.md and every EJE document ever committed
searches.method: Read in full; searched for numbered rules and for rule headings
searches.result: Contains requirements, decisions, mandates and process rules PROC-1…PROC-5 — no rule register numbered 1-27.
Commit messages reference change IDs, never rule numbers.

searches.method: All 124 owner-written messages separated from 13 machine-written compaction summaries, then searched for rule headings and numbered lists
searches.result: Found rules 1-10 (twice, differing) and 25-27. Nothing numbered 11-24. Recovered instead: the founding instruction's 14 ARCHITECTURAL PRINCIPLES and the CR-12 instruction's MOST IMPORTANT RULE.

searches.source: Project conversation — pasted and queued instructions
searches.result: Task instructions only. No rule register.

searches.method: All 34454 transcript records JSON-decoded and every string walked, searching for numbered lists that reach 11-24 with imperative wording
searches.result: Six such lists exist in the whole project history. Five are task requirement lists; the sixth is the founding ARCHITECTURAL PRINCIPLES, already recovered. No rules 11-24.

searches.method: Included in the full decoded scan above (every record type, not only user messages)
searches.result: No rule register. Nothing was read from a file that no longer exists.

searches.method: Searched /root/.claude and /home/user for CLAUDE.md, AGENTS.md, memory and instruction files; grep for rule numbering
searches.result: Only the EJE repository's own CLAUDE.md/AGENTS.md, which point at the Next.js docs and carry no project rules.

searches.method: The uploaded authoritative business scope document, never previously opened. Extracted word/document.xml in full (354 paragraphs, 21812 characters) and searched every numbered item and heading
searches.result: DECISIVE: its items 11-24 are topic headings (Checklists, Parts Delivery Note, Media and Technical Library, …), not rules. The document contains no rule register, no mention of "tracker" and no mention of "tablet friendly", so it is not the source of rules 25-27 either. RECOVERED FROM IT: 17 standing rules, verbatim — §2 Product objective and principles (9) and §28 Development control rule (8).

searches.method: Compared every recorded wording and classified each by how it introduces itself
searches.result: Three wordings exist. Phase 2 §7 is register-framed ("The established rules include:"); the BD-06 preamble is task-scoped (its rule 2 says "in this task"); Phase 3B §4 is a description ("the known wording currently recorded"). None is demonstrably the owner's verbatim original.

searches.method: Phase 3A and Phase 3B wordings compared character by character
searches.result: Rules 25 and 26 identical in both. Rule 27 differs by one word: "accommodate" (3A) against "accomidate" (3B, stated twice). The Phase 3B wording is recorded and the earlier one kept as a variant.
